clue.text: Opening for a routine over in A&E

indicators.note: in places the following pieces between the two letters of the hospital department's name

parts.note: A&E is the hospital Accident and Emergency department, giving its two letters A and E
per means for a or for each, as in per head

indicators.note: over tells us the word for a routine is turned round

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a slot in the busy schedule of a hospital's accident and emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is Britain's hospital casualty department; 'for a' means per, as in a price per person, and 'over' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, a synonym for an opening.

clue.text: A range of Parisian designs

indicators.note: of signals that the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A collection of fashions from Paris designers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a product line; it is a mountain range, sitting across parisiAN DESigns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are a mountain range in South America, an example of a range.

clue.text: He's earned bucks as a songwriter

indicators.note: bucks as a verb means jerks about like a horse, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A songwriter boasts of the dollars he has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' reads as dollars but is the anagram signal working on HESEARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Sheeran is a British singer known for writing his own hit songs, an example of a songwriter.

clue.text: Drink then scrap over Russian teams

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells us both words just named are read from the bottom up

parts.note: saki is a spelling of sake, the Japanese rice wine
an ort is a scrap of food left over

explanation.surface: A boozy evening followed by a brawl involving Russian sports teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SAKIORT round to TROIKAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a team of three horses pulling a Russian sledge or carriage.

clue.text: Perhaps a fraction of The Sound of Music?

parts.note: a sound mind is a sane or rational one
a number is a piece of music, a song in a show

explanation.surface: Asks whether a snippet of the famous musical is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sound of Music is a stage and film musical, but here sound means sensible and a musical piece is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Any fraction of two whole numbers, such as three quarters, is an example of this kind of value.

clue.text: Still cold in 7

indicators.note: in places the letter for cold within the fabric word

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is material, and plaid is a tartan fabric
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Something remains chilly inside the material.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 7 points to the answer at 7 down, so a kind of that is needed: PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid water is calm and unmoving, so still is a synonym.

clue.text: Office bug — it's been caught

indicators.note: been caught says the little word is trapped inside the illness word

parts.note: the lurgy is British slang for a mild unspecified illness, a bug
the clue gives it as written, with 's standing for has

explanation.surface: A virus is going round the workplace and someone has caught it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace but is a church service; THE LURGY is a British jokey name for any bug going around.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a form of church service, and a liturgy is the set form of public worship.

clue.text: Make thick, hard material

parts.note: to clot is to thicken into lumps, as blood or cream does
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce a dense, tough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth is woven fabric, a synonym for material in the dressmaking sense.

clue.text: Withdraw money in error — remove clothes

indicators.note: in tells us the word for error goes inside the word for undressing

parts.note: to divest is to strip off clothing
a sin is a wrong or moral error

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out cash by mistake and then strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinvest is to pull capital out of a company or venture.

clue.text: Bond character filling out note in conference?

definitions.text: Bond character filling out note in conference?

parts.words: Bond character filling out note in conference?
parts.note: Michael Bond wrote about a bear from Peru who arrived in London wearing a label note; padding means filling out

explanation.surface: A James Bond figure fills in paperwork during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is not 007 but Michael Bond, author of the children's books; padding is filling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Bond created the marmalade-loving bear named after a London railway station, his best-known character.

clue.text: Play dead and one's left

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
one is I, and the 's adds S
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone acts dead and the others have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to frolic or amuse oneself, a literary synonym for play.

clue.text: Fancy talk, so it has produced no answer

definitions.text: Fancy talk, so it has produced no answer

parts.words: Fancy talk, so it has produced no answer
parts.note: the clue is all talk and no wordplay, illustrating the proverb that deeds count for more than speech

explanation.surface: A grumble that elaborate chatter has achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the clue itself is only words and gives no mechanism, which is the proverb's point.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says deeds matter more than talk, so fine speeches that achieve nothing prove it.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
Bowl with wood, soft, like

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
B marks a soft pencil lead, as in 2B
as in means like or for example

explanation.surface: A list of materials for a wooden bowl, soft and similar.
explanation.walkthrough: B for soft comes from pencil grading, where B leads are soft and black.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a bowl for washing hands and face, so bowl is a broader term for it.

clue.text: Bugger off, as can anyone

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude invitation to get lost, open to anyone who wants it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugger off' reads as a swear phrase, but 'Bugger' alone is the definition and 'off' the anagram signal on CANANYONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bugger can be a nuisance or pain, something irritating.

clue.text: Ancient oil in the ground, and carbon

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Old oil deposits underground, along with carbon, as a geology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is the past tense of grind, rearranging OILINTHE into NEOLITHI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic was the New Stone Age, so things from it are very old.

clue.text: Poem about one black hat

indicators.note: about says the poem word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem
un is a dialect form of one, as in a good un
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A poem on the subject of a single dark hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbonnet is a brimmed cotton bonnet worn against sunlight, a kind of hat.

clue.text: Yellow, say, on a climbing herb

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
eg means for example, which is what say means here

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the two words are read upwards

explanation.surface: A yellow plant, for example, climbs a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ONA up to ANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant herb of the mint family, much used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Border guards love to get on

indicators.note: guards means holds protectively inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: to abut is to border on or adjoin
love is zero in tennis, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: A frontier patrol protects a romance so it can go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link phrase joining wordplay to the definition 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A book about birds is one on birds, so the two words share the sense concerning.

clue.text: Poor slumber is one of our problems

definitions.text: Poor slumber is one of our problems

parts.words: Poor slumber is one of our problems
parts.note: poor is a typical signal for rearranging letters, so poor slumber is itself a rearranging puzzle for solvers, giving rumbles

explanation.surface: A crossword solver complains of bad sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: 'Poor slumber' is exactly this kind of puzzle device, and crosswords are our problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging another's letters is a staple puzzle device for solvers.

clue.text: Such optimism may be a trap, of course

definitions.text: Such optimism may be a trap, of course

parts.words: Such optimism may be a trap, of course
parts.note: a bunker is a sand trap on a golf course, so a cast of mind can be a trap in two senses

explanation.surface: A warning that positive thinking can lead you astray.
explanation.walkthrough: On a golf course a BUNKER is a sand trap; optimism is a mindset, and this defensive mindset is the opposite, so the clue is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege mindset of defensive pessimism, the reverse of hope, is a frame of thought like optimism.

clue.text: Composition one saw upside-down

indicators.note: upside-down in a down clue means the saw word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tenon saw is one kind of saw, used for joinery

explanation.surface: Someone saw a musical score held the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see; it is the tool, the tenon saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical piece written for nine players, so it is a composition.

clue.text: A long time that is wasted in kiss

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill

indicators.note: wasted in means the little word is lost from inside the next one

explanation.surface: Years spent on a single kiss that came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IS from KISS by 'wasted in' leaves KS; YONKS is British slang for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is informal British slang for ages, a very long period.

clue.text: State capital wants unlimited cuts secured

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the trimmed word goes inside the word for secured

parts.note: safe means secure or protected

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A capital city demands unrestricted spending cuts be locked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as spending reductions but means slices into; 'unlimited' drops the outer letters of wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of the US state of New Mexico.

clue.text: Get to keep the clay

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: to earn is to get or gain money

explanation.surface: Someone gets to take the pottery clay home.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes things made of baked clay, such as pots, so clay used as an adjective fits.

clue.text: One into unacceptable belief

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the phrase for unacceptable

parts.note: not on is an informal phrase for unacceptable
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone enters a view no one can accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or opinion someone holds, a synonym for belief.

clue.text: I'm into a lovely threesome — looks painful!

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the trio's name

parts.note: the three Graces are the goddesses of beauty and charm in Greek myth
the clue gives it as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A boast of joining a lovely trio, then wincing at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovely threesome' sounds racy but is the three Graces of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimaces are twisted facial expressions showing pain or disgust, so painful looks.
